text: Although aerobic exercise can be carried out using a variety of modalities, running and cycling have primarily been studied in the context of concurrent training. The meta-analysis by Wilson and colleagues (79) revealed that running had a particularly negative effect on the hypertrophic adaptations associated with resistance training, whereas cycling did not appear to cause a significant detriment. The authors speculated that running-related impairments on muscle growth could be related to excessive muscle damage caused by its high eccentric component. Conceivably, this could inhibit recuperative abilities and thus blunt the post-exercise adaptive response.
